leverage.exposure: No leveraged position is open right now. The balance is positive and the matchday-five deadline passed clean with cash in hand, exactly eleven players and a legal formation. The recommended flips would deliberately open a large negative balance, which is the single thing on this page that can cost an entire matchday if it is mishandled: a negative balance at matchday start scores zero across the board. Two things make it tolerable here and neither is optional. First, the deficit sits comfortably inside the floor, which is measured as a fixed share of team value and therefore grows with every purchase. Second, there are six days and several ticks between the unwind and the lock, so there is ample time to sell the flipped players back — which pays exactly market value with no spread — and return to a non-negative balance and exactly eleven players. The flips must never reduce the fielded eleven, and the unwind must be complete before the lock, not near it. If the evening tick goes against the position, do not panic-sell into it: there are further ticks before the deadline and the squad itself is untouched either way.

binding_gap: There is no formation gap. Eleven players fill a 4-4-2 exactly and all eleven are placed, so nothing is binding in the sense that costs points this matchday. What is binding is quality, not shape: the cheapest defender is a bench body whose average is the lowest in the side by a wide margin, and he is in the eleven only because the squad has no twelfth man. That is a supply problem — the board has not offered a fit, starting defender worth buying — and it does not improve by forcing a purchase. Leave it until the board offers one.

verdict.headline: Quiet points market, wide-open value market.
verdict.headline_short: Quiet points market, wide-open value market.
verdict.detail: Quiet points market, wide-open value market. The squad is unchanged, legal and fully fielded, nobody is hurt, and there is no points buy on the board worth making — so there is nothing to do on the points side at all. The whole of this run's value sits in the three flip calls carried over from last night, all three still listed at exactly market value with the rising flag intact. They are a single correlated bet, not three independent ones, because all three players kick off at the same time today and all three are paid out by the same evening tick. Place them, do not raise, and unwind back to eleven players and a non-negative balance well before the matchday locks — there are six days of slack to do it in, which is the only reason a leveraged position is tolerable here at all.

sell.reason: No sale is recommended. With the squad at exactly eleven, every sale would drop the side below a fillable formation and trigger the penalty unless a replacement lands first, and no replacement on the board is worth buying. The only sales this run contemplates are the unwind legs of the flips, which sell newly-bought players back to Kickbase and return the squad to exactly eleven — those are not squad sales and cost no points.

buy.reason: Nothing on the board is a points buy. The one listing that would genuinely have upgraded the weak defender slot — a meaningful jump in average points for a modest net outlay — fails the fitness check on a source dated yesterday, and nothing newer contradicts it, so the avoid stands; absence of news resolves against the buy, not for it. His listing expires late this morning in any case. The remaining defenders on the board are either carrying a status flag, barely rated, or already on the blocked list from an earlier sale. The rest of the board is attackers and midfielders for slots already covered. Do not pad.

movers.reason: The flip window is wide open and the mechanism re-measured this run with no decay at all — the rising-flag edge is, if anything, wider than the prompt's standing figures now that the sample has roughly doubled, and the falling flag remains a reliable mirror image. Three Kickbase board listings qualify: all three are board postings with no manager ask anywhere on the market, all three are priced at exactly market value, all three carry the rising flag and a clean status, and all three pass the two-clock test with room to spare — each auction expires today, the tick that pays it fires this evening, and the matchday lock is six days after that. Bid exactly market value on each and never raise; losing an auction costs nothing, while chasing one into the contested cluster destroys the edge outright. The new finding this run is that all three players kick off at the same hour today and the single evening tick that pays all three lands a few hours after they finish. The measured drift already contains post-match ticks, so that is not an argument against the trade — but it does mean the three outcomes are correlated through one tick and one matchday. Treat it as one position, not three. Sequencing matters: the two larger listings expire within the hour before dawn and fit inside the static envelope as it stands, while the third expires in the afternoon and only fits because each purchase enlarges the envelope as team value rises. So place the first two now and place the third after they have resolved, when the capacity is actually there. If the platform refuses the third for budget, that costs nothing and the first two stand on their own. Two questions remain open and unresolved, as they have been: whether Kickbase caps squad size, which would cap how many flips can run at once, and the fact that this edge is measured in one league over one period and will decay if rivals crowd in. Rivals here flip the daily tick constantly, including on unavailable players — which for a pure value flip is correct, since fitness does not enter the tick.

fitness.sweep: Clean sweep, no flags anywhere. The live injury and suspension table carries none of the eleven squad players and none of the three flip targets, and the connector agrees — every squad row and every target carries a clear status. Nobody is newly injured, suspended, benched, or carrying dated news that he might leave the league. The transfer check on the flip targets passes on its own terms as well: the German window is shut, and the two targets with any recent transfer noise at all are both on dated record committing to their current clubs. One correction for the record: the largest of the three flip targets plays for Stuttgart, not Gladbach as an earlier entry stated — the price and mechanics in that call are unaffected, only the club label was wrong.
